title: Hagwon Resignation Receipt Room
oneLiner: A contract-exit evidence room for Korea hagwon teachers deciding what to sign, what to document, and how to escalate without losing wages.
targetUser: Foreign teachers in Korean hagwons facing resignation papers, contract amendments, wage issues, or MOEL escalation decisions.
keyUX: Enter contract dates, upload or mock employer messages, mark wage/housing/visa risks, check proof completeness, and choose sign/wait/escalate with a handoff memo.
sourceSignals: S9 - Reddit r/teachinginkorea hagwon resignation/contract uncertainty: https://www.reddit.com/r/teachinginkorea/
S10 - Korea small merchants/labor policy pressure context: https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/06/01/small-business-owners-deepen-pressure-labor-policy-change-and-rising-costs/5611780368680/
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app called "Hagwon Resignation Receipt Room" for foreign teachers in Korean hagwons facing resignation papers, contract amendments, wage issues, or MOEL escalation decisions. The app is based on observed user pull: teachers already compare contract dates, screenshot employer messages, ask Reddit whether to sign, contact MOEL, and collect wage or housing proof before making a risky decision. The app should use a pre-signature evidence room mechanic around the trigger moment "an employer asks the teacher to sign a resignation or amended contract today" and make the first screen communicate "Do not sign before your proof is in order." Use the user's own language: "They want me to sign today, but I need to know what proof to save first." Build the core workflow around contract dates, employer messages, wage status, housing/visa risk, resignation document, MOEL notes, and translation questions, and produce a pre-signature evidence receipt plus escalation memo. Required sections: signature pressure header, contract timeline, employer message and document vault, wage/housing/visa risk lanes, MOEL proof checklist, sign/wait/escalate decision matrix, translation note cards, and exportable evidence receipt. Emotional pressure to make visible: 역전, wage leverage, visa fear, employer pressure, and shame of being cornered alone. Design direction: use the `operator-dense` profile with compact charcoal/fog evidence panels, crisp known/unknown status chips, severe signature-deadline accents, dense document rows, and no decorative hero. Avoid generic dashboard framing; make the main interaction feel like a calm evidence room that slows down a bad signature decision.
